test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 19 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Mass is the amount of matter in an object
The SI units of weight and mass are the same

solution:
The correct answer is __**Mass is the amount of matter in an object**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mass** is defined as the fundamental measure of the **amount of matter** contained within an object. It is an intrinsic property that does not change regardless of the object's position in the universe. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• **Weight** is the force exerted on an object due to **gravity**. It is calculated using the formula **W = m × g**, where 'm' is mass and 'g' is the acceleration due to gravity. Therefore, weight is directly dependent on the gravitational pull of the location. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The **SI unit of mass** is the **kilogram (kg)**, while the **SI unit of weight** is the **Newton (N)** because weight is a measure of force. Since they represent different physical quantities, their units are not the same. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **mass** of an object remains **constant** throughout the universe unless matter is physically added to or removed from the object. It does not fluctuate based on altitude, latitude, or different celestial bodies. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• While **mass** is a **scalar quantity** (having only magnitude), **weight** is a **vector quantity** because it has both magnitude and a direction pointing towards the center of gravity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Gravitational Variations:**
 
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity (g)** on **Earth** is approximately **9.8 m/s²**. However, on the **Moon**, gravity is about **1/6th** of that on Earth.
 
• Consequently, an object with a **mass** of **60 kg** will have a weight of **588 N** on Earth but only about **98 N** on the Moon, even though its **mass** remains exactly **60 kg**.
 
 
 
• **Measurement Tools:**
 
 
• **Mass** is typically measured using a **physical balance** or a **beam balance**, which compares an unknown mass with a known standard mass.
 
• **Weight** is measured using a **spring balance**, which measures the extension of a spring caused by the gravitational pull on the object.
 
 
 
• **Inertia:**
 
 
• **Mass** is also a measure of **inertia**, which is the resistance of an object to any change in its state of motion. The greater the **mass**, the higher the **inertia**, making it harder to accelerate or stop the object.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Center of Gravity:** This is the point through which the entire **weight** of a body acts. For a regular-shaped object with uniform density, this point usually coincides with its geometric center.
 
• **Zero Weight:** An object can experience **weightlessness** (zero weight) in **free fall** or in **deep space** far from any celestial body, but its **mass** can never be **zero** as long as it exists as matter.
 
• **Relativistic Mass:** According to **Albert Einstein's** theory of relativity, the **mass** of an object can appear to increase when it travels at speeds approaching the **speed of light**, though for all general science and classical mechanics applications, mass is considered **constant**.
